Hi, thanks for the updates, but this way of creating a copy is not sufficient. The issue with calling `std::string::c_str()` is that you loose all perks that come with C++ RAII or automatically garbage collected languages. Once the function `read()` is terminated `copiedData` will be freed. This means that the data pointed to by `c_str()` is also no longer available. Maybe it is not immediately apparent because after `IfcFile::Init()` the majority of data is parsed and present in memory. Strings and enumerations are parsed lazily and would probably crash in this approach. Additionally, once the IfcFile is freed it will try to clean up the `c_str()` which will not work, because it already has been freed or because it was allocated in a different way internally by the `std::string`. This is likely the error you report about. Long storey short, you really need to use the `memcpy()` approach used here: https://github.com/IfcOpenShell/IfcOpenShell/blob/master/src/ifcgeomserver/IfcGeomServer.cpp#L490

Usage of this type would allow any developer who imports of `ifcopenshell` to for example write methods like this:
```py
from functools import reduce
from ifcopenshell.file import file as IfcFile
from ifcopenshell.util.constants import IFC_TYPES

def get_names_of_entities_by_types(
  f: IfcFile,
  types: set[IFC_TYPES],
  /,
) -> list[str]:
  """
  Obtains all entities by a given set of types
  and returns the names of these elements
  """
  # get all entities
  entities = reduce(
    lambda x, y: x + y,
    map(lambda t: f.by_type(t), types),
    []
  )
  # get names
  names = map(lambda e: getattr(e, "Name", None), entities)
  # filter out null-values
  names = filter(lambda name: isinstance(name, str), names)
  # return list
  return list(names)
```

You're right to question it — removed `SA_NODEFER`. 

Without `SA_NODEFER`, SIGSEGV/SIGBUS are automatically masked while the handler executes. Since we call `sigsetjmp(..., 1)` (with `savesigs=1`), the signal mask is saved at the `sigsetjmp` point and restored by `siglongjmp`. So the flow is:

1. `sigsetjmp` saves current mask (signals unmasked)
2. Signal fires → handler runs with SIGSEGV masked (safe)
3. `siglongjmp` restores saved mask → signals unmasked again
4. `SigGuard` destructor restores original handlers

With `SA_NODEFER`, if `siglongjmp` or subsequent code triggered another fault, the handler would re-enter and potentially infinite-loop. Removing it is strictly safer.

* `path.outline` Partially correct. When there are two faces sharing an edge, one facing the camera, and the other edge-on or facing away. So it marks the silhouette, but also contours.
* `path.boundary` Wrong. A boundary is where an edge only has one face. It is where an object is not a closed, manifold mesh.
* `path.crease` Wrong. When the two faces sharing an edge form a valley with a great enough angle.
* `path.sharp` Wrong. When the two faces sharing an edge form a ridge with a great enough angle.
* `path.flush` Wrong. When the two faces are not coplanar, but do not pass the threshold to make them a crease (valley) or sharp (ridge) they are set to flush.

Sources:
- libstdc++ defines `__cpp_lib_to_chars` from GCC 11 ([charconv, gcc-11.1.0](https://github.com/gcc-mirror/gcc/blob/releases/gcc-11.1.0/libstdc%2B%2B-v3/include/std/charconv#L47-L48)). The MSVC STL completed `<charconv>` in VS 2019 16.4 ([what's new in VS 2019](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cpp/overview/what-s-new-for-cpp-2019?view=msvc-170)) and defines the macro in [yvals_core.h](https://github.com/microsoft/STL/blob/main/stl/inc/yvals_core.h).
- libc++ has floating-point `to_chars` since LLVM 14, but it still does not define `__cpp_lib_to_chars` (it is commented out in [`<version>` up to LLVM 21](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/blob/llvmorg-21.1.0/libcxx/include/version#L374)), so the feature-test macro on its own would turn the fast path off on every libc++. libc++ 18+ instead has `_LIBCPP_AVAILABILITY_HAS_TO_CHARS_FLOATING_POINT`, which is 0 when the deployment target is below macOS 13.3 / iOS 16.3 ([18.1.0](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/blob/llvmorg-18.1.0/libcxx/include/__availability#L210-L218), [21.1.0](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/blob/llvmorg-21.1.0/libcxx/include/__configuration/availability.h#L298)). libc++ 14 to 17 keep the snprintf search: they have no equivalent 0/1 macro, and 14 to 16 mark the overloads unavailable on Apple whatever the target.

So the current macOS builds (deployment targets 10.15 in `nix/build-all.py`, 10.13/11.0 in conda) stay on the search, as before. Emscripten now takes the `to_chars` path, because its libc++ has no availability gate.
